xref.title: Daft Punk Origins – Darlin' 1992; Melody Maker Called Them "Daft Punky Trash"; Became Daft Punk
xref.body: Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo (full first name: Guillaume Manuel) is from just west of Paris; his great-great-grandfather was a famous Portuguese military figure and his grandfather a famous Portuguese poet. Thomas Bangalter is from Paris; his father was a songwriter and record producer and Thomas started piano at age six. The two met in high school in 1987 and formed the rock band Darlin' (named from a Beach Boys song they covered) in 1992. Darlin' recorded four songs, played two gigs, and lasted six months before dissolving after a Melody Maker review called them "daft punky trash" — that phrase became their new name. The third member of Darlin', Laurent Boutonnat, went on to work with Phoenix. "Owing to that snarky review and melody maker, they started Daffed punk."

xref.title: Saturday Night Live Performance (March 27, 1997)
xref.body: The Tragically Hip appeared as a special musical guest on Saturday Night Live on March 27, 1997, performing two songs, including "Nautical Disaster." This high-profile national US television exposure was facilitated by Kingston native Dan Aykroyd, who was seen wearing a Tragically Hip t-shirt in the 1992 movie *Sneakers*. Despite this major vehicle, the performance did not result in a significant breakthrough in the American market. "That was one of two songs they performed on Saturday Night Live on March 27th, 1997. ... The answer is Dan Acroid. Dan is from Kingston. In fact, if you go back to the movie Sneakers with Acroid and Robert Redford and Ben Kingsley, Sydney Ponce, and River Phoenix in 1992, you'll see Dan wearing a tragically hip t-shirt under a sport coat."

xref.title: Addiction Philosophy and Social Circle
xref.body: John Frusciante's perspective on his addiction was intrinsically linked to his depression, leading him to believe he should be perpetually on drugs because they brought him happiness. He explicitly stated, "I was very sad and I was always happy when I was on drugs. Therefore I should be on drugs all the time. I was never guilty. I was always proud to be an addict." During this period, his social circle included many drug-using companions, notably the actor River Phoenix, who would soon die, and Al Jourgensen. "I was very sad and I was always happy when I was on drugs. Therefore I should be on drugs all the time."

xref.title: Early Life and Birthplace
xref.body: Chester Bennington was born on March 20, 1976, in Phoenix. His mother was a nurse, and his father was a police detective whose work primarily focused on child sex abuse cases. "Chester was born on March 20th, 1976 in Phoenix."

xref.title: Early Phoenix Bands
xref.body: Before moving to Los Angeles to audition for Hybrid Theory (which became Linkin Park), Chester Bennington was active in the Phoenix music scene. Around age 17 in 1993, he sang in a band with his friend Sean, initially "Sean Dattel and his friends?" and then co-formed Gray Daze, which existed from late 1993 through 1998. "We now turn our attention to the parts that came together to form Lincoln Park, specifically what Chester Bennington was up to in Phoenix before he was invited to move to LA to sing for this new group."

xref.title: Early Tour Bus
xref.body: In their early days, Green Day's first tour bus was an old library bookmobile bought from the Phoenix School system. It was overhauled by drummer Tré Cool's father, Mr. Wright, who owned a small trucking company. Mr. Wright generously acted as the official driver for the band's first three tours. "Drummer Trakewool's father came in really handy back then because he owned a small trucking company and he overhauled this old library bookmobile that he had bought from the Phoenix School system."

xref.title: Gray Daze Frustration
xref.body: Despite Gray Daze being a local sensation in Phoenix, releasing two indie albums ("Wake Me" in 1994 and "No Sun Today" in 1997) and opening for international acts, they failed to attract major record labels. Burned out and discouraged, Chester quit the group in 1998, contemplating giving up music altogether, until he received the call to audition for Hybrid Theory. "So burned out and discouraged, Chester quit the group in 1998, and thought about giving up music called together."

xref.body: The Congos brothers grew up in both South Africa and London before eventually moving to Phoenix. Coming from a musical family, they began performing together as Congos in 2007 while still living in South Africa. "John Congos' sons grew up in South Africa and London before moving to Phoenix. And coming from an obviously musical family, they started performing as Congos in 2007 while they were still in South Africa."

xref.title: Local Sensation Without Major Label Interest
xref.body: Gray Daze, which existed from late 1993 through 1998, became a genuine local sensation in Phoenix, opening for international acts. However, despite their popularity, they were unable to attract the interest of any major record labels. "Gray Days was a genuine local sensation, but for some reason they could not get any of the large record labels interested in what they were doing."

xref.title: Merkin Vineyards and Caduceus Cellars – Maynard James Keenan's Arizona Wine Operations
xref.body: Maynard James Keenan owns Merkin Vineyards and Caduceus Cellars, high-end wine operations located in the Sedona area of Arizona, specifically in Cornville, north of Phoenix and south of Flagstaff off I-17. He invested money earned from Tool and A Perfect Circle into these ventures. Merkin refers to a wig worn in the pubic region, while Caduceus, the ancient symbol for commerce, is associated with the brand's website, www.cadocious.org. His wines, particularly the '84 cab blend, have received excellent reviews, and the tasting center invites wine lovers to sample and purchase. "Maynard owns Merckin Vineyards."

xref.title: Opening for The Rolling Stones
xref.body: While working on "A Den of Thieves" in Toronto in Summer 2005, rumors surfaced about The Rolling Stones rehearsing for a secret show. Larry Wanigas, unable to get tickets, instead secured The Trews an opening slot at The Phoenix with just 24 hours' notice, contingent on Charlie Watts' health. The band was sworn to secrecy and, upon arriving for soundcheck, found The Rolling Stones already on stage. They earned a photo with the legendary band after their set. "Larry calls... I can't get you tickets, but you can open for them."
